name: MathlibAnnex.Matrix.ballVolumeScaledMaximalMinors
title: Maximal minors scaled by the reference ball volume

content.display_title: Maximal minors scaled by the reference ball volume
content.one_sentence_role: Fixes the volume factor and increasing-row signs.
content.natural_language_statement:
Let $n,N\in\mathbb N_0$ and give $E=\mathbb R^n$ and $F=\mathbb R^N$ their coordinate sup norms. Let $\lambda_n$ be the fixed coordinate Lebesgue measure on $E$. Let $p:E\to\mathbb R$ be a continuous real seminorm with specified constants $a_p,b_p>0$ such that
$$a_p\|x\|_\infty\le p(x)\le b_p\|x\|_\infty\qquad(x\in E).$$

The lower bound makes $p$ a norm. Its closed unit ball and real reference volume are
$$K_p=\{x:p(x)\le1\},\qquad v_p=\lambda_n(K_p)\in(0,\infty).$$
Here and below a finite Lebesgue measure is read as a real number when used as a scalar.

Let $A:E\to F$ be linear. Index its maximal minors by increasing row selections $I=(i_1<\cdots<i_n)$ from $\{1,\ldots,N\}$, using $A_{ij}=(Ae_j)_i$. Write $\Pi_n(A)$ for the vector of these maximal minors and $\mathcal V_p(A)$ for its volume-scaled version. They are given by
$$\mathcal V_p(A)=v_p\Pi_n(A),\qquad(\mathcal V_p(A))_I=v_p\det(A_{i_a,j})_{a,j=1}^n.$$
content.definition_explanation:
This definition multiplies every maximal minor by $v_p$. Increasing row order fixes each determinant sign. [The real ball-volume definition](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/MeasureTheory/Measure/EquivalentSeminormBall.lean#L18-L19) takes the finite measure $\lambda_n(K_p)$ and reads it as the real scalar $v_p$. The volume is finite and positive because
$$\{x:\|x\|_\infty<1/b_p\}\subseteq K_p\subseteq\{x:\|x\|_\infty\le1/a_p\}.$$
The first inclusion puts zero in the interior ([interior-point lemma](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Module/EquivalentSeminorm/Topology.lean#L35-L46)); continuity makes the ball closed and the second bounds it, giving [compactness](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Module/EquivalentSeminorm/Topology.lean#L26-L33). Positivity of Lebesgue measure on a nonempty open set and finiteness on compact sets give [finite positive ball volume](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/MeasureTheory/Measure/EquivalentSeminormBall.lean#L21-L28).
content.assumptions: The source and target are finite real coordinate spaces with sup norms. The seminorm $p$ is continuous and has the stated positive lower and upper comparison constants. The measure is the original coordinate Lebesgue measure. No contraction assumption is imposed on $A$. The dimensions $n,N$ may be zero. When $n=0$, the unique empty minor has determinant $1$; when $N<n$, the minor-index set is empty and its function space has one element. Neither case is excluded.
content.conclusion: The output is a real vector with one coordinate for each increasing row selection $I$. The reference coordinates and measure stay fixed.
content.lean_realization_notes: Every linear map between these finite-dimensional spaces is continuous. The type of the source therefore does not narrow the stated class of maps.
